result.topic_en: An inserted page with Euler's attempted proofs that 2 is a quadratic residue of primes 8q+7 and that 3 is a residue of primes 12q+11, plus marginal notes on the prime divisors of 8xx-1.
result.transcription:
64 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.

Pagina intercalata.

Tentamen demonstrationis, quod si divisor primus sit $8q+7$, in residuis reperiatur 2. Ponamus esse in residuis 2, et cum ibidem sit $(2q+m)^2$, erit quoque $8qq+8mq+2mm$, hincque
$8mq+2mm-7q$ et $2mm-7m-7q$ et $2mm-7m+q+7$,
quod si nunquam fiat non-residuum, patebit propositum. At non-residua repraesentari possunt per quadrata negativa, quorum dupla etiam erunt residua per hypothesin; sit ergo
$2mm-7m+q+7=-2aa+8bq+7b$, fietque
$q=\frac{2aa+2mm-7m+7-7b}{8b-1}$ et $8q+7=\frac{(4a)^2+(4m-7)^2}{8b-1}$,
foretque $8q+7$ divisor ipsius $(4a)^2+(4m-7)^2$, quod cum fieri nequit, sequitur ex residuo 2 nullum deduci absurdum, cujusmodi necessario resultare deberet, si 2 non esset residuum. (*)

Theorema. Si divisor $12q+11$, erit 3 residuum.
Ponamus 3 esse residuum, ac si nullum absurdum inde sequatur, pro vero erit habendum. Erit ergo $-3$ non-residuum, et omnia non-residua $-3aa$. At residuum est $(2q+m)^2$ et $12qq+12mq+3mm$, hincque $3mm-11q-11m$, item $3mm+q-11m+11$, quod nunquam potest esse non-residuum $-3aa$: ponatur enim
$3mm-11m+11+q=-3aa+12bq+11b$, erit
$q=\frac{3aa+3mm-11m+11-11b}{12b-1}$, unde fit $12q+11=\frac{(6a)^2+(6m-11)^2}{12b-1}$,
quod cum sit absurdum, $3mm-11m+11+q$ nunquam inter non-residua continebitur.

Vel ita pro divisore $8q+7$.

Si 2 esset non-residuum, in genere $2mm-7m-7q\pm\alpha(8q+7)$ esset non-residuum; in genere autem residuum est $(4q+n)^2=16qq+8nq+nn=8nq+nn-14q=nn-14q-7n=nn+2q-7n+14\pm\beta(8q+7)$, omnes ergo numeri continerentur in alterutra harum formularum:
$2mm-7m-7q\pm\alpha(8q+7)$
$nn-7n-14q\pm\beta(8q+7)$.
Si unicus assignari posset numerus, hic non contentus, demonstratio esset perfecta; vel si idem numerus in utraque contineretur, quod fit si, posito $m=f+g$, $n=f+2g$, fuerit $ff-2gg+7g+7q$ divisibile per $8q+7$.

(*) Script. ad marg. Si $2mm-7m+q+7$ ponatur $=-aa$, fit
$8q+7=\frac{2(2a)^2+(4m-7)^2}{8b-1}$,
nunc demonstrandum restat $2xx+yy$ nunquam divisibile esse per $8q+7$.
Nota altera, ut videtur, huc pertinens. $8xx-(2y+1)^2$ alios divisores primos non habet, nisi formae $8n-1$ et $8n+1$
$\frac{8xx-1}{7}$ int si $x=7a\pm1$, $\frac{8xx-1}{23}$ int. si $x=23a\pm7$, $\frac{8xx-1}{31}$ int. si $x=31a\pm2$
$\frac{8xx-1}{47}$ " " $x=47a\pm10$, $\frac{8xx-1}{17}$ " " $x=17a\pm7$, $\frac{8xx-1}{41}$ " " $x=41a\pm6$.

methods.what: Attempted proof that 2 is a quadratic residue mod a prime 8q+7 by showing that assuming 2 is a residue yields no contradiction
Attempted proof that 3 is a quadratic residue mod a prime 12q+11, via a sum of two squares divisibility argument
Alternative approach: classify all numbers mod 8q+7 into residue and non-residue quadratic forms
Condition for a number to lie in both forms
Prime divisors of 8xx-(2y+1)^2 are of form 8n±1, with explicit congruence classes of x for 8xx-1

items.quote: si divisor primus sit $8q+7$, in residuis reperiatur 2
items.english: If the prime divisor is 8q+7, 2 is found among the residues.
If the divisor is 12q+11, 3 will be a residue.

items.quote: foretque $8q+7$ divisor ipsius $(4a)^2+(4m-7)^2$, quod cum fieri nequit
items.english: and 8q+7 would be a divisor of (4a)^2+(4m-7)^2, which cannot happen

items.quote: Si unicus assignari posset numerus, hic non contentus, demonstratio esset perfecta
items.english: If a single number could be assigned that is not contained here, the proof would be complete.

items.quote: nunc demonstrandum restat $2xx+yy$ nunquam divisibile esse per $8q+7$.
items.english: It now remains to prove that 2xx+yy is never divisible by 8q+7.

items.quote: $8xx-(2y+1)^2$ alios divisores primos non habet, nisi formae $8n-1$ et $8n+1$
items.english: 8xx-(2y+1)^2 has no prime divisors other than those of the form 8n-1 and 8n+1.
